To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the shaping method is more efficient than conventional learning in the presence of a teacher and (ii) shaping is most efficient for complex tasks and when the teacher is able to provide feedback on the sub-components of the task.

shaping significantly boosts the speed and stability of acquisition of a hierarchical working-memory task, and that this is achieved by the learner decomposing the task in a similar way as the teacher.

shaping can be a powerful learning method, but that the success of shaping depends on the structure of the target task, the teacher’s ability to decompose that task into smaller components, and the learner’s ability to acquire these components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the computational mechanisms of shaping, and the conditions under which they are most effective.
the role of shaping as a method of instruction in cognitive development and its computational modeling.
shaping as a method for teaching complex skills, and we provide a computational framework for understanding its benefits.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
shaping works by breaking the task into small steps, and by providing the learner with the opportunity to practice each sub-component of the task in isolation.
the shaping method is a powerful and flexible tool that allows the teacher to control the learner’s acquisition of a complex task.
shaping is a powerful method to speed up the learning of tasks with a high temporal complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
shaping is a powerful method of instruction, but it is not a panacea.
shaping is a flexible and powerful tool for instruction.
shaping helps to learn complex tasks by providing a more gradual and flexible way to acquire them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shaping can be used to teach a complex task to a learner by providing it with a sequence of sub-goals that can be acquired by trial and error.
shaping can be used to decompose a complex task into a sequence of simpler tasks, and this decomposition can be done in a variety of ways, each of which has different advantages.
a flexible shaping strategy that allows the teacher to adapt to the current state of the learner can be more efficient than a rigid strategy that follows the same steps in each training trial.
